column2: Those who delight in needless meat-eating go to a hell of caustic mud; then they are cast down by elephants, falling as by the wind.
At the end of that they are born again with defective limbs. He who does not approach his own wife in her fertile season, O lord of men,
goes to the dreadful Raurava and incurs the guilt of Brahmin-slaying. One who sees another engaged in wrongdoing and, being able, does not prevent him,
incurs that sin, and both go to hell. One who tallies sinners' sins and reports them to others also incurs sin.
If the charge is true, they are alike in sin; if false, the sin is doubled, O king. One who falsely charges a sinless man with a sin and reviles him
goes to a terrible hell for as long as moon, sun and stars last; half the sin of the sinners who are reviled is destroyed.
One who takes up vows and abandons them unfinished suffers in the Sword-leaf Forest and is born on earth with defective limbs.
A man who obstructs the vows being undertaken by others goes to a very painful, terrible hell where he eats phlegm.
One who shows partiality in judgment and in teaching of dharma has no atonement even with ten thousand penances.
One who eats forbidden food obtains excrement as food; then, born in a Chandala womb, he becomes always an eater of beef.
One who insults Brahmins with words incurs Brahmin-slaying; after suffering all the tortures, he is a Chandala for ten births.
One who causes obstruction while a gift is being given should perform the vow equal to Brahmin-slaying.
One who seizes something and gives it to others for the sake of a gift — the thief goes to hell; the fruit belongs to the owner of the property.
One who promises and does not give goes to the "saliva-eating" hell; one given to reviling ascetics, O king, goes to the Shilanamatra hell.
Those who cut down gardens go for twenty-one ages; then they suffer, in order, all tortures, eating dog-food.
Hear the fate of those who break temples, tanks, O king, and flower-gardens.
They are cooked separately in all those tortures; then they are worms in excrement for twenty-one kalpas.
Then for a hundred births they are born in a Chandala womb, O king: destroyers of villages, burners and plunderers.
I cannot describe their great sin within my lifetime. Those who eat leavings and those who betray friends
suffer sharp tortures as long as moon and stars last; those who cut off ancestral rites and offerings to gods, and stand outside the path of the Veda.
Of sins and tortures and of dharmas as well, O king, there are many kinds of tortures for evildoers.
I am not able to count them. Of sins, tortures and dharmas, O king,
who in the world can tell the number without Vishnu? When, according to dharma-scripture, the expiations are performed for all these sins,
the mass of sin is destroyed. Expiations should be done near the Lord of Lakshmi,
to complete any deficiency or excess in the rites. The Ganga, tulsi, company of the good, praise of Hari,
freedom from envy and non-violence — all of these remove sin. Acts offered to Vishnu become fruitful;
acts not offered are like goods placed in ashes. Daily, occasional, desire-motivated rites and any other means to liberation,
if offered to Vishnu, become sattvic and fruitful. Supreme devotion to Hari destroys all sin of men.
That devotion is to be known as tenfold, like a forest fire for the forest of sin: tamasic, rajasic and sattvic, O best of kings.
Worship of the Lord of Lakshmi for the destruction of another is the lowest tamasic devotion, as it carries the nature of malice.
One who worships Narayana, the lord of the world, with a deceitful mind, like a wanton wife her husband — that is middling tamasic.
Seeing others devoted to worship of gods, one who worships Hari out of envy — that devotion, O king, is called the best tamasic.
One who worships Hari asking for wealth and grain, with supreme faith, is called the lowest rajasic.
One who worships Madhava with great devotion wishing for fame renowned in all the worlds — that is held to be middling rajasic.
One who worships Hari aiming at a state like sharing his world and the rest — that is called the best rajasic devotion, O king.
One who worships Hari to destroy his own sins, with supreme faith, is held to be the lowest sattvic.
One who serves, thinking "this is dear to Hari," with faith, is the middling sattvic.
One who worships the Lord of Lakshmi as a servant would, thinking it a duty, O king, is the foremost of devotions, the best sattvic.
The man who delights in doing something for Hari's glory and is content in being absorbed in him — that devotion is the best of the best.
I alone am the Supreme Vishnu; in me is all this world — whoever constantly sees thus should be known as the best of the best.
For what purpose I have come near you, O lord of men, I shall tell you, O wise one; listen with attention.
Thus devotion is tenfold, cutting off samsara; and among them sattvic devotion gives the fruit of all desires.
Therefore, O king, hear, you who desire to conquer samsara: devotion to Janardana should be practised without contradicting one's own duty.
One who abandons his own dharma and lives by devotion alone — Vishnu is not pleased with him; he is pleased by right conduct.
Conduct is the first thing considered in all scriptures; dharma springs from conduct, and the Lord of dharma is Achyuta.
Therefore devotion to Hari should be practised without conflict with one's own dharma. For those without good conduct, even dharmas give no happiness.
Devotion without one's own dharma is declared as if not done. I have now told all that you asked.
Therefore, intent on dharma, worship Janardana, Narayana, the subtlest, and you will attain lasting happiness.
Shiva is Hari himself, and Hari is Shiva himself; the wicked who see a difference between them go to hell by the millions.
Therefore worship Vishnu and Shiva with equal mind; one who makes a distinction suffers sorrow here and hereafter.
Your grandfathers, sinners who killed themselves, burned by Kapila's wrath, dwell in hell, O king.
Rescue them, O fortunate one, by bringing the Ganga; the Ganga destroys all sins, O king.
Hair, bones, nails, teeth and ash, O best of kings, when touched by Ganga water, she leads to Vishnu's abode.
He whose bone or ash is cast into the Ganga by men, O king, is freed from all sins and goes to Hari's abode.
Whatever sins have been told to you, O king, all these deeds are destroyed by being sprinkled with a drop of Ganga water.
Sanaka said: Having said this to the great king Bhagiratha, the soul of dharma, the Lord of Dharma, O tiger among sages, at once vanished.
That wise king, master of the meaning of all scriptures, entrusted the whole earth to his ministers and went to the forest.
Going to the snowy mountain, to the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, in the west on a peak covered with snow, sixteen yojanas across,
he performed austerity and brought down the Ganga, purifier of the three worlds.
Filled with exceeding joy, with hair standing on end and voice choking, he cried out "Krishna, Krishna, Shri Krishna!"
Vishnu, pleased in heart, the inner controller, teacher of the world, the Lord who cares for beings, spoke, moved by compassion.
The Lord said: O fortunate Bhagiratha, your wish will be fulfilled; your forefathers will come to my world.
O king, praise Shambhu, another form of mine, with hymns by your own power; he will at once fulfil all your desires.
He who seized the moon that had come for refuge — therefore worship Ishana, giver of happiness, with hymns of praise.
The god without beginning or end, giver of the fruit of all desires, worshipped by you, O king, will at once bring about your good.
Having said so, the Lord of the lords of gods, the master of the worlds, Achyuta, vanished, O best of sages; and the king rose up.
Was this a dream, or was it truly seen, O best of Brahmins? The king, in wonder, thought, "What shall I do?"
Then in the sky a voice spoke to him, whose mind was confused: "This is true; you should not worry."
Hearing this, the king, intent on devotion, praised Ishana, the cause of all, the king of all gods.
Bhagiratha said: I bow to the Lord of the world, destroyer of the distress of those who bow, the god beyond the reach of proof, Ishana, whose nature is Om.
Whose form is the world, unborn, eternal, the cause of creation, preservation and dissolution; O Virupaksha of universal form, I bow to you of fierce vigour.
The greatest of yogis know him, without beginning, middle or end, infinite, unborn, imperishable, as the increaser of nourishment; I praise him.
Homage to the lord of the worlds, to the one who deceives and deludes; homage to Nilagriva, homage to the lord of beings (pashupati).
Homage to the one with a skull in hand, lord of the bonds; homage to the form beyond conception, lord of the elements.
Homage to the one who holds the Pinaka bow, to the trident-bearer; homage to the one with a skull in hand, who bears the noose and the mace.
